newsitem.title: CONGO: Shelling, gunfire endanger Congo Brazzaville truce.
newsitem.headline: Shelling, gunfire endanger Congo Brazzaville truce.

text.p: Artillery fire boomed across the Congolese capital Brazzaville on Monday and witnesses said it was the worst since the start of a precarious truce on June 17.
The shelling and gunfire threatened to undermine efforts by the local mediator, city mayor Bernard Kolelas, to prevent a return to all-out hostilities.
The truce, negotiated as French troops left the city after evacuating foreign nationals and then extended for a week, had stopped political and ethnic clashes that began on June 5.

No day has gone by without some firing, blamed by mediators on rogue elements in the two rival forces, supporters of President Pascal Lissouba or of his predecessor, former military leader Denis Sassou Nguesso.

The two men and Kolelas, whose supporters have stayed out of the fighting, were the main contenders in presidential elections that had been due on July 27 but have been postponed indefinitely because of the fighting.
The United Nations is trying to put together a mainly African intervention force for Brazzaville, but has insisted that the truce must first be rigidly observed.
